prompt: In the `Fields` demo the student picks *Spanish* from the course `<select>`. What does `course` hold?
hint: Look at the JSON the demo printed, and at the options' attributes.

choices.text: `"Spanish"`, the text the student saw on the screen
choices.why: That is what an option with no `value` would give. These options all have one.

choices.text: `1`, the option's place in the list
choices.why: A select hands over a value, not a position; the position is not stored anywhere.

choices.text: `"spanish"`, the option's `value`
choices.why: Right. The value is the id and the text is the title, the planner's rule for every list.

choices.text: The `<option>` element that was chosen
choices.why: `v-model` holds data, never an element; an element is what a template ref gives.

prompt: The student empties the `Minutes` field of `Fields.vue`, an `<input type="number" v-model="minutes">`. What does `minutes` hold now?
hint: Vue converts what it can convert, and leaves the rest.

choices.text: `0`, since an empty number field counts as zero
choices.why: Vue never invents a zero; an empty field would then pass a rule that only checks the range.

choices.text: `NaN`, the result of a conversion that failed
choices.why: A conversion that fails leaves the original value rather than writing `NaN`.

choices.text: `null`, to say the field has no value
choices.why: Vue writes what the field gives, and an empty field gives text, not `null`.

choices.text: `""`, an empty string
choices.why: Right. Only what parses becomes a number; the table says an empty field gives `""`.

prompt: Which of these fields hand `v-model` a value that is not a string, with no modifier? Choose all that apply.
hint: Only one field type is converted by Vue on its own; the other way is to bind the value yourself.

choices.text: `<input type="number">` holding 45
choices.why: Right. Vue reads the field's `type` and converts it to a number.

choices.text: `<input type="date">` holding the 30th of October
choices.why: A date field gives `"2026-10-30"`, a string, which is the format the planner already uses.

choices.text: A `<select>` whose options bind `:value` to numbers
choices.why: Right. Bound with `:value`, the option hands over whatever you gave it, a number included.

choices.text: Radio buttons with `value="reading"` and `value="practice"`
choices.why: A plain `value` attribute is text, so the radio gives the string of the one chosen.

prompt: In the first run of the `Modifiers` demo, `lazy` stayed `""` although `verbs` had been typed. In the second it showed `"verbs"` after Tab. Why?
hint: Which event does each kind of `v-model` listen to?

choices.text: `.lazy` waits a short delay after the last key, and the first run ended too soon
choices.why: There is no timer in `.lazy`. It waits for an event, not for time to pass.

choices.text: `.lazy` writes on `change`, which fires when the field is left
choices.why: Right. Without it `v-model` always writes on `input`, once per key.

choices.text: `.lazy` writes when the form around the field is submitted
choices.why: There was no form in the demo; leaving the field was enough.

choices.text: Tab re-rendered the page, and the ref had been written all along
choices.why: The ref was empty until the focus left: the first run printed it while it still was.

prompt: A text field has `v-model.number="minutes"` and the student types `abc`. What does `minutes` hold?
hint: Read what the lesson says `.number` does with a value that does not parse.

choices.text: `NaN`
choices.why: That is what `parseFloat` returns, and Vue does not write it: it checks for it.

choices.text: `0`, the number it falls back to
choices.why: There is no fallback number; inventing one would hide the mistake.

choices.text: The string `"abc"`
choices.why: Right. A value that does not parse is left as it was: `.number` checks nothing, so it is a convenience and not validation.

choices.text: `""`, because the modifier refuses what is not a number
choices.why: `.number` refuses nothing. Refusing is the validation's job, a few sections on.

prompt: A course title saved as ` Guitar`, with a space in front, sorts first and never matches a search. Written as `v-model.___`, the field stores `Guitar`.
hint: The modifier that removes spaces at the ends.

prompt: What does `useId()` give each copy of `FormField`?
hint: Two fields of one form are two copies of the same component.

choices.text: The component's name, shared by the copies
choices.why: Then two fields would share one id, and a label would reach the wrong input.

choices.text: An id unique on the page, for its label and its error to point at
choices.why: Right. The capture shows `v-0`, and the message's `v-0-error` is built from it, so every copy is joined to its own parts.

choices.text: A random id drawn again on every render
choices.why: An id that changed on every render would detach the label between two renders; it is fixed per copy.

choices.text: The `id` the parent wrote on `<FormField>`
choices.why: The parent writes none in this lesson; the component makes its own.

prompt: Remove `inheritAttrs: false` and `v-bind="$attrs"` from `FormField`, and keep `type="number" min="5"` on the parent's tag. Where do those two attributes end up?
hint: Lesson 6's fallthrough picks one element of the component.

choices.text: On the `<input>`, the first element inside the component
choices.why: Fallthrough does not look for an input; it uses the root element.

choices.text: They are dropped, as a component keeps its declared props and discards the rest
choices.why: Undeclared attributes are not dropped: that is exactly what fallthrough is.

choices.text: Vue refuses to compile a component given attributes it never declared
choices.why: Vue accepts them and passes them on; nothing fails, which is why the mistake is easy to miss.

choices.text: On the wrapping `<div class="field">`, so the input stays a text field
choices.why: Right. The root gets them, and a `<div>` with `type` does nothing.

prompt: In `FieldContract`, `1.5` is typed into the hours field. How many minutes does `minutes` hold afterwards?
hint: The writable computed's setter multiplies by 60 and rounds.

prompt: Why does the form have `shown` as well as `errors`?
hint: One answers what is wrong; the other answers what to say.

choices.text: `errors` is recomputed on submit, and `shown` keeps it fresh in between
choices.why: `errors` is a computed, so it is never stale; it is current at every keystroke.

choices.text: `errors` is always current; `shown` stays empty until the first submit
choices.why: Right. An untouched form is not greeted with three red messages, and after one try each one disappears as it is fixed.

choices.text: `shown` caches `errors`, so the rules run once instead of on every key
choices.why: A computed already caches; `shown` exists for when to speak, not for speed.

choices.text: `shown` holds the sentences for the screen, `errors` short codes
choices.why: Both hold the same sentences; `shown` is `errors` or nothing.

prompt: The form has `novalidate`, yet the minutes field still carries `min="5"` and `max="240"`. What are they there for?
hint: `novalidate` stops one thing the browser does with them, not everything.

choices.text: The browser still blocks a submit outside the range, as a second check
choices.why: Blocking the submit is precisely what `novalidate` stops.

choices.text: Vue reads them to write the message *Between 5 and 240 whole minutes.*
choices.why: The message is written by hand in `errors`; Vue never reads `min` or `max`.

choices.text: The arrows of the number field, and the range a screen reader announces
choices.why: Right. They describe the field; `novalidate` only stops the browser's bubble.

choices.text: They are left over from before `novalidate` was added
choices.why: They still do two jobs, both for the student rather than for the check.

prompt: Which values of `draft.minutes` make `errors.minutes` a message? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three conditions: whole, at least 5, at most 240.

choices.why: Right. Below the minimum of 5.
The rule is `<= 240`, so four hours exactly is allowed.
Right. Inside the range, but `Number.isInteger` refuses it: whole minutes only.

choices.text: `""`, from an emptied field
choices.why: Right. An empty number field gives a string, and a string is not an integer.
The rule is `>= 5`; the minimum itself passes.

prompt: The form was submitted with the course empty and 500 minutes. In the HTML it printed, which control had neither `aria-invalid` nor `aria-describedby`?
hint: Which field had nothing wrong with it?

choices.text: The course `<select>`
choices.why: It was empty, so it carried both, pointing at *Choose a course.*

choices.text: The date field
choices.why: Right. It held today, so it was fine, and a field with nothing wrong is never marked.

choices.text: The minutes field
choices.why: 500 is above 240, so it was marked and described by `v-2-error`.

choices.text: None of them: a failed submit marks every field of the form
choices.why: Each field is marked from its own error, not from the submit; the date had none.

prompt: What does `aria-describedby="v-2-error"` on the minutes input do for a screen-reader user?
hint: Look at the table: one attribute names, one marks, one describes.

choices.text: It names the field, as `<label for>` does
choices.why: The label names the field; the description comes after the name.

choices.text: It moves the focus to the message when the submit fails
choices.why: No attribute moves the focus; the planner moves it only after a success, with a template ref.

choices.text: It reads the message after the field's name and value
choices.why:
Right. The field points at the `

` by id, so the message is heard every time the field is reached.

choices.text: It announces the field as invalid when it is reached
choices.why: That is `aria-invalid`'s job, the attribute beside it.

prompt: A colleague's form sets `aria-invalid="true"` on every empty field from the start, and removes it as each one is filled. What goes wrong?
hint: Think of the student who has not touched anything yet.

choices.text: The student notices no change: `aria-invalid` is ignored until a message exists
choices.why: A screen reader announces it whether or not a message is there.

choices.text: Every field is announced as wrong on the first visit, before anything was typed
choices.why: Right. It is the screen-reader version of greeting a fresh form with three red messages.

choices.text: The browser blocks the submit, because `novalidate` covers `min` and `max` and not ARIA
choices.why: `aria-invalid` is for assistive technology; the browser's own checks never read it.

choices.text: The `role="status"` line reads the errors aloud as the page opens
choices.why: The status line says only what it is given, and nothing writes errors into it.

prompt: Why does `submit()` set `saved.value = ''` before returning on an invalid form?
hint: What would the status line still say from the session before?

choices.text: So an old *Added…* line does not linger over a new failure
choices.why: Right. Nothing should say a session was added when none was.

choices.text: So the live region reads the errors out instead
choices.why: Nothing writes errors into the status line; each field announces its own when reached.

choices.text: Because `role="status"` refuses a new text while the form is invalid
choices.why: The role refuses nothing; it announces whatever the paragraph is given.

choices.text: It is step four, the reset for the next entry
choices.why: The reset happens only after a success; this is the early return of step two.

prompt: After a successful submit the course is cleared and the minutes go back to 30. Why is the date left as it was?
hint: Think of the next session the student adds.

choices.text: The date came in as a prop, and a component cannot write to its props
choices.why: It was copied into `draft` once; the draft is the form's own, and it could be reset.

choices.text: Clearing it would show *Choose a date.* at once
choices.why: `tried` goes back to false in the same reset, so nothing would show.

choices.text: A student planning a day adds its sessions one after another
choices.why: Right. The reset keeps what the student would type again, and nothing else.

choices.text: `Object.assign` cannot set a property back to a string
choices.why: It sets `course` back to the string `''` on the line itself, as any reset would.

prompt: Guitar was added on the 24th, for 25 minutes. How many minutes did the week's footer then say were planned?
hint: The line under the week's list: `75 of … minutes done`.

prompt: The form now sends each session to a server, and the request fails. What should the form do, as the lesson describes?
hint: The student should not have to type everything twice.

choices.text: Clear the fields, so the next try starts clean
choices.why: Clearing makes the student type the whole session again for a failure that was not theirs.

choices.text: Say so in the status line, and keep what was typed
choices.why: Right. The same line that says *Added…* says what failed, and the student tries again with every field as it was.

choices.text: Set `tried` back to false and hide the messages
choices.why: `tried` is about the student's own mistakes; a failed request is not one.

choices.text: Disable the button until the page is reloaded
choices.why: The button is disabled while sending, not after; a reload would lose every ref.

prompt: In `SessionForm`, how does the course `<select>` get the field's id and the id of its message?
hint: The select is not `FormField`'s own `<input>`; it is content the form hands in.

choices.text: Through `$attrs`, which `inheritAttrs: false` sends on to it
choices.why: `$attrs` goes to the default `<input>`; the select is not that element.

choices.text: By calling `useId()` itself, which repeats the id within one form
choices.why: Each call gives a new id; calling it again would detach the select from its label.

choices.text: Through provide and inject, from the form down to each field
choices.why: Nothing is provided here; the values travel one level, from the field to its slot.

choices.text: From the scoped slot, which hands it `id`, `invalid` and `describedBy`
choices.why: Right. Lesson 7's scoped slot: the field passes the three values, and the select wires them; nothing else is needed.

prompt: Pressed empty, the planner's form showed only *Choose a course.* Why not the other two messages?
hint: What were the date and the minutes when the form opened?

choices.text: A form shows the message of its first invalid field and no other
choices.why: Every invalid field shows its own; the 500-minute capture showed two at once.

choices.text: The date started as today and the minutes as 30, both within the rules
choices.why: Right. Only the course had no starting value.

choices.text: Only the select is checked on submit; inputs are checked as they are typed in
choices.why: All three rules sit in one computed, and `shown` reveals all of them on the first submit.

choices.text: `shown` reveals one more error each time the button is pressed
choices.why: `shown` is all of `errors` or nothing at all.

prompt: Put what happens on a valid submit in the order the planner does it.
hint: Stop, check, act, reset; the focus moves last.
items: `tried` is set to true and `valid` is checked
The store is handed a copy of the draft
The status line says what was added
The course is cleared and the minutes go back to 30
The focus returns to the course field

prompt: Match each attribute of the planner's form to what it does.
hint: One description is something the planner deliberately does not do.

pairs.right: Marks the field as wrong when it is reached
Has the message read after the field's value
Announces a new line without moving the focus
Keeps the browser's bubble from blocking the submit

right_distractors: Moves the focus to the first invalid field

prompt: On a component, `v-model` is a prop plus a listener for `update:modelValue`. In the child, both halves are written as one call to the macro `___()`.
hint: The same call `FormField` makes on its third line of script.

prompt: A new `FormField` for a session's title has the rule `title: draft.title ? '' : 'Write a title.'`. A student types three spaces and the rule lets them through. What on the parent's `v-model` would catch them?
hint: A modifier on a component is applied to the value the component emits.

choices.text: `.trim`, so the three spaces arrive as `""`
choices.why: Right. Vue applies the modifier to all that `FormField` emits, and an empty string fails the rule: none of the spaces get through.

choices.text: `.lazy`, so nothing is written until the field is left
choices.why: On leaving, `.lazy` writes the three spaces all the same; it changes when, not what.

choices.text: `.number`, which turns text that is not a number into `""`
choices.why: `.number` leaves text that does not parse as it was, spaces included.

choices.text: None: a modifier works on `<input>` and is lost on a component
choices.why: The `.number` on the hours field in `FieldContract` worked through a component; `.trim` does too.
